missingCandidates.title: An Atomic-Scale Chemical Switch for Oxide Ferroelectricity
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Interfacial chemistry offers new opportunities for designing ferroelectric materials, yet their coupling with intrinsic polarization remains largely unexplored. Here, we synthesize ferroelectric BiFeO3 nanoparticles with {100} facets covered by a Bi2FeO6-x Aurivillius-like phase, allowing the interfacial Bi2O2 layer to interact with bulk polarization at different relative orientations. Using atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, we observed a large polarization enhancement when the interface aligned with the bulk polarization, and a polarization reversal when opposing it. In situ heating and first-principles calculations show that the Bi2O2 layer repels the underlying FeO6 octahedra, which either rotate or rigidly displace to accommodate the chemical stress, depending on local geometry. Moreover, this mechanism can imprint local polarization in Aurivillius phases and nonferroelectric oxides, offering a general route to design polar topologies in oxide heterostructures.

missingCandidates.title: Wavelength-Selective Magneto-Optical Diodes Based on Rare-Earth Chiral Molecular Crystals
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Chiral materials, integrating structural breaking of mirror-symmetry, exhibit physical properties that cannot be observed in centrosymmetric analogues. Among these properties, optical magneto-chiral anisotropy, the nonreciprocal absorption of light shown by chiral magnetized systems, is emerging as an enabling technology in magneto-optics and photonics. Here, we report on enantiopure chiral molecular crystals based on the erbium(III) rare-earth ion that display nonreciprocal, wavelength-selective, magnetic field-induced variations of the optical absorption coefficients up to ca. 200% for the intrashell f–f electronic transition falling in the 1.5 μm telecom wavelength range. Such a response is associated with an exceptionally high Magneto-Chiral Dichroism induced by the strong spin–orbit coupling of the Er(III) and the helical chirality at the lanthanide center, exalted by the magnetic-dipole-allowed character of the electronic transition. This chirality-induced nonreciprocal magneto-optical response represents a proof of concept for the use of these chiral crystalline molecular materials as potential components in magneto-optical diodes.

missingCandidates.title: Cascade Remodeling through Late-Stage Electrophilic Fluorination in a Bis-Spiroketal Framework
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Cascade reactions efficiently generate molecular complexity but are often incompatible with the late-stage diversification of highly functionalized natural products due to competing degradation pathways. Herein, we demonstrate that electrophilic fluorination can serve as a variable control element, selectively capturing transient nucleophiles to install fragment-deactivating C–F bonds that redirect subsequent reactivity away from default degradation. In a derivative of the antibiotic salinomycin, sequential fluorination events gate a multistep structural cascade, converting a single precursor into diverse, unprecedented scaffolds. Stepwise reagent selection enables divergent cascade routing through enol ether manifolds to achieve controlled scaffold remodeling. These results demonstrate late-stage electrophilic fluorination as a switchable fragment-deactivation strategy for directing complex cascade transformations and unlocking new natural product architectures.

missingCandidates.title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03 , a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -( G03 )- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

missingCandidates.title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

missingCandidates.title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

missingCandidates.title: Direct Enantioselective α-Alkoxylation of β-Keto Esters Enabled by Umpolung Strategy
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Chiral ethers adjacent to a carbonyl group represent a valuable class of motifs; however, their catalytic asymmetric synthesis from readily available carbonyl compounds remains underexplored. Here, we present a catalytic asymmetric umpolung C–O bond-forming reaction of β-keto esters with alkyl hydroperoxides. This protocol employs in situ activation of alkyl hydroperoxides with trichloroacetonitrile, enabling the enantioselective alkoxy transfer to β-keto esters under catalysis by a chiral bifunctional organocatalyst, thereby allowing access to a broad range of highly functionalized, enantioenriched ethers bearing quaternary stereocenters.

missingCandidates.title: Enantioselective Pericyclization of Naphthol-Substituted Alkynyl Ketimines
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract A vinylidene ortho-quinone methide (VQM)-mediated, organocatalyzed tandem 6π-azaelectrocyclization and dearomatizing spirocycloaddition of naphthol-substituted alkynyl ketimines, facilitated by NBS, have been realized. This strategy enables the enantioselective synthesis of axially chiral 3-haloquinolines and previously unexplored spirocyclic xanthenopyrroles under mild conditions, with excellent functional group tolerance and high efficiency. Significantly, this represents the first intramolecular method for constructing axially chiral biaryl quinolines via 6π-azaelectrocyclization of naphthol-substituted alkynyl ketimines. Furthermore, a range of downstream transformations highlights the broad synthetic utility of these halogenated heterobiaryls.

missingCandidates.title: Visible-Light-Induced Three-Component CH2 Insertion and Trifluoroethylation of Quinoxalin-2(1 H )-ones
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Quinoxalin-2(1H)-ones represent an important class of nitrogen-containing heterocycles. We have developed a three-component strategy enabling the insertion of a methylene (CH2) unit, which was successfully applied to the trifluoroethylation of quinoxalin-2(1H)-ones. In this reaction, trifluoromethylsulfonyl-pyridinium (TFSP) served as the trifluoromethyl source and acetone provided the CH2 moiety, thereby introducing trifluoroethyl at the C3 position of quinoxalin-2(1H)-ones. This method is distinguished by its broad substrate scope with good yields, metal-free and mild reaction conditions, and remarkable step economy that seamlessly cascades C–H alkylation, trifluoromethylation, and deacetylation. Gram-scale experiments confirmed its practicality for potential large-scale applications. The reaction mechanism was systematically investigated, with key intermediates experimentally captured and characterized and further corroborated by DFT calculations.

missingCandidates.title: Mild Heterogeneous Thiophene Hydrogenation Enabled by a Modified Palladium Catalyst
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Thiophenes are readily available sulfur heteroarenes and prominent motifs in medicinal and synthetic chemistry, but their direct heterogeneous hydrogenation to thiolanes remains challenging due to sulfur-induced catalyst deactivation and competing hydrodesulfurization. Here, we report a chloroform-induced surface modification strategy that enables the heterogeneous Pd(OH)2/C-catalyzed hydrogenation of thiophenes to saturated sulfur heterocycles. The method proceeds under mild hydrogenation conditions and provides access to a range of alkyl-, silyl-, aryl-, and benzofused thiolane derivatives. A hydrogenation-focused robustness assessment revealed compatibility with several functional groups that are commonly sensitive under Pd/H2 conditions, while preparative scope studies showed that functional-group-containing thiophenes can be converted when potentially interfering motifs are separated from the thiophene core by suitable alkyl or aryl spacers. Mechanistic experiments indicate that CHCl3 is not merely a beneficial solvent: CHCl3/H2 pretreatment of Pd(OH)2/C generates a catalytically competent material whose activity is retained after replacing CHCl3 with 2-MeTHF. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) analyses support the formation of persistent chloroform-derived organochlorine/C–Cl-type surface environments and chlorocarbon fragments. These findings establish solvent-induced catalyst modification as a useful design principle for challenging heterogeneous hydrogenations of sulfur-containing heteroarenes.

missingCandidates.title: Cooperative Agostic‐Type C─H···Cu, Quadrupolar Cu···CO 2 , and C─H···O/π Interactions in an Ultra‐Microporous MOF Enable One‐Step Methane Purification From Quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT While agostic‐type C─H···metal σ‐interactions are central to organometallic catalysis, their role in gas separation remains elusive. In this study, a robust phosphine‐functionalized ultra‐microporous Cu(I/II)‐organic framework, LIFM‐XYY‐15, featuring open metal sites (OMSs) and rich aromatic pore walls, is designed to enable one‐step CH 4 purification from a quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4 mixture. Notably, LIFM‐XYY‐15 exhibits much higher C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 uptakes than CH 4 , showing C 3 H 8 /CH 4 , C 2 H 6 /CH 4 , and CO 2 /CH 4 uptake ratios of 2.46, 2.30, and 3.92 at 298 K and 1 bar, respectively, which are significantly raised to 12.18, 8.59, and 9.89 at 0.1 bar. The separation potentials (∆ q ) reach 22.12 (C 3 H 8 /CH 4 ), 20.34 (C 2 H 6 /CH 4 ), and 43.69 (CO 2 /CH 4 ) cm 3 cm −3 at 298 K and 1 bar, demonstrating excellent CH 4 purification ability from the quaternary mixture. Breakthrough experiments confirm the delivery of high‐purity CH 4 (≥99.9%) with a productivity of 1.39 mol L −1 with excellent recyclability. The in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD), in situ FT‐IR spectroscopy, and molecular simulations reveal that the exceptional selectivity arises from the synergistic interplay of agostic‐type C─H···Cu, quadrupole‐electrostatic Cu···‐CO 2 , and alkane C─H···O/π interactions, which collectively reinforce the affinity for C 2 –C 3 hydrocarbons and CO 2 while disfavoring CH 4 . This work discloses a crucial role of agostic‐type interactions as a powerful yet underexplored design principle for selective hydrocarbon separations.

missingCandidates.title: Electrochemical Control of Scholl Reaction: Arenium Cation Versus Radical Cation Pathways
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The Scholl reaction is a cornerstone method for constructing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, yet its mechanism remains highly debated because arenium and radical cation intermediates are difficult to characterize. Herein, we demonstrate that electrochemical oxidation provides precise mechanistic control: a low‐potential acidic (LPA) condition selectively favors the arenium cation pathway, whereas a high‐potential neutral (HPN) condition promotes the radical cation pathway. While it is often assumed that only one mechanism operates under a given set of chemical oxidation conditions, our results reveal that most substrates can react via both pathways. Dialkoxyphenyl groups are found to facilitate the radical cation pathway, although no general correlation with overall substrate electron richness is observed. This electrochemical control provides the experimental basis to re‐evaluate previously proposed mechanisms for certain substrates. We demonstrate that switching between LPA and HPN conditions yields different products from the same 3,3’‐diphenyl‐2,2′‐binaphthalene substrate, thereby correcting the computational assignment of the corresponding pathways. Additionally, we show that a tetracene‐derived substrate undergoes cyclodehydrogenation through the arenium cation pathway, revising the computationally assigned dication mechanism for this transformation. Collectively, these results establish electrochemistry as a powerful alternative to traditional chemical oxidation, offering unprecedented experimental control to resolve fundamental mechanistic debates about the Scholl reaction.

missingCandidates.title: Fan Hong
Neutrophil Extracellular Trap‐Mimetic DNA Nets Enable Concurrent Bacteria‐Targeted Eradication and Toxin Neutralization
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Current antibacterial therapies often suffer from limited bacterial selectivity, host‐cell toxicity, and inflammation triggered by toxin release during bacterial killing. Here, we report a neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)‐mimetic, dopamine‐incorporated DNA net, termed D A Net‐DA, enabling targeted bacterial eradication and concurrent toxin neutralization. Inspired by the trap‐kill‐neutralize function of NETs, D A Net‐DA selectively captures and traps bacteria, followed by in situ catalytic formation of polydopamine nanoshells on the trapped bacteria. This process enables efficient photothermal bacterial eradication while minimizing damage to host cells. Meanwhile, the nanoshells act as molecular sponges to sequester and neutralize bacterial toxins, thereby mitigating toxin‐associated inflammation. These integrated functions endow D A Net‐DA with potent therapeutic efficacy in vivo, as demonstrated by markedly reduced bacterial burdens, toxin levels, tissue inflammation in both conventional and burn wound infection models. Moreover, the simultaneous clearance of bacteria and residual toxins alleviates pro‐inflammatory macrophage polarization, thereby accelerating wound tissue regeneration. This work presents a NETs‐mimetic antibacterial strategy that integrates pathogen clearance with toxin neutralization, offering a promising method for treating bacterial infection‐associated diseases.

missingCandidates.title: Programming Hydrophobic Nanocavity of DNA Frameworks for Ultrastable Fluorescent Imaging
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorescent proteins (FPs) are widely used in biological imaging, yet their limited programmability restricts adaptability for advanced nanoscale applications. Synthetic molecular containers offer designable cavities but struggle to simultaneously achieve large dimensions, biocompatible interfaces, and precise microenvironment control. Here we report DNA framework (DNF) dots, highly programmable fluorescent probes constructed by encapsulating Cy3 within three‐dimensional DNA‐encoded hydrophobic nanocavities. Using amphiphilic tetrahedral DNA frameworks with inward‐oriented alkyl chains, we create well‐defined nanocavities (4.8–8.9 nm) with tunable size, shape, and internal chemistry. Single‐molecule analysis reveals that DNF dots enhance photostability (up to 15‐fold) and total photon output (up to 58‐fold), as compared to single Cy3 tagged on single‐stranded DNA. The exceptional photostability and brightness of DNF dots enable stable binding event frequencies exceeding 7500 frames in DNA‐PAINT super‐resolution imaging. Furthermore, integration into light‐inducible DNA hydrogels yields rewritable information encoding platforms. DNF dots thus establish a versatile platform that combines the environmental shielding of fluorescent proteins with the programmability of synthetic molecular containers, introducing a DNA framework‐encoded microenvironment engineering paradigm for ultrastable fluorescent probes.

missingCandidates.title: Red Light‐Gated Charge Transfer Enables Trace Oxygen Response in Dye‐Sensitized TiO 2 –Carbon Nanotube Hybrids
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Light offers a powerful means of activating materials with spatial and temporal precision. However, translating excited‐state processes into chemically responsive electronic function in conductive solids remains challenging, particularly under low‐energy red illumination. Herein, we report red light‐gated charge transfer in dye‐sensitized single‐walled carbon nanotube–TiO 2 (SWCNT–TiO 2 ) hybrids that enables trace oxygen detection. Immobilization of red‐absorbing squaraine sensitizers on TiO 2 domains embedded within a conductive SWCNT network reversibly generates a photostationary charge‐transfer state under 628 nm excitation. Despite the low photon energy of red light, the hybrid architecture supports interfacial electron injection into TiO 2 and hole accumulation in the nanotube scaffold, while remaining electronically dormant in the dark. Interception of photogenerated electrons by O 2 perturbs this light‐induced state and converts excited‐state redox chemistry into a chemiresistive signal with ppb‐level sensitivity. This capability enables continuous monitoring of oxygen depletion in a sealed headspace during food spoilage. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, energy‐level alignment analysis, and charge‐carrier inversion experiments show that O 2 triggers light‐activated changes in SWCNT carrier density. These findings demonstrate that low‐energy optical excitation can gate chemical response in dye‐sensitized SWCNT–TiO 2 hybrids, establishing a design strategy for temporally controlled sensing and photoresponsive electronic function.
topics: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment

missingCandidates.title: Resolving the Sensitivity–Specificity Trade‐Off in Fluorescent Probes via a Tandem‐Activatable Shielding Strategy
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT For precise tumor diagnosis, the intrinsic trade‐off between sensitivity and specificity in fluorescent probes remains a longstanding bottleneck, underscoring an urgent need for strategies to break this fundamental constraint. To address the specificity limitation, we exploited a highly polarity‐sensitive fluorescent scaffold to construct a tandem‐activatable probe, enabling sequential activation by the acidic tumor microenvironment and the angiogenic marker aminopeptidase N. Whereas the single‐locked counterpart is prone to premature activation in circulation, the tandem‐locked probe remains inactive owing to a maleamic acid‐based shielding unit and is activated only upon encountering these two tumor hallmarks. Furthermore, this shielding strategy increases probe hydrophobicity, enhancing tumor uptake and driving accumulation of released fluorophores in low‐polarity lipid droplets, where fluorescence is markedly amplified to improve imaging sensitivity. The probe exhibits rapid and specific activation across various solid tumors with minimal toxicity, thus effectively resolving the sensitivity‐specificity trade‐off in probe design for in vivo applications.

missingCandidates.title: V─O─Ti Bridge‐Bond Polarity Boosts Na + Migration in V‐Based Fluorophosphates for Fast Sodium Storage
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Vanadium‐based fluorophosphates are promising high‐energy‐density cathodes for next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, the pronounced degradation of Na + diffusion at high voltage hinders their fast‐charging capability. Herein, a Ti 4+ ‐doping‐induced bridge‐bond‐polarity‐driven strategy is proposed to reshape the V electronic structure for facilitating V─O electron exchange. Correspondingly, voltage hysteresis, polarization, and structural distortion at high voltage are suppressed, accompanied by enhanced electronic conductivity. Meanwhile, the polar V─O─Ti bridge bonds expand the dominant one‐ and two‐dimensional Na + transport channels by inducing bridging‐O displacement, further boosting Na + migration capability. Therefore, Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 with V─O─Ti delivers high capacities of 121.8 and 62.1 mA h g −1 at 0.1C and 50C, respectively, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Additionally, the 0.92‐Ah Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 //HC pouch cell exhibits 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1C. At the 9 Ah scale, the pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 154 Wh kg −1 . This synergistic reinforcement strategy driven by bridge‐bond polarity paves the way for sustainable high‐power polyanionic SIBs.

Herein, we report red light‐gated charge transfer in dye‐sensitized single‐walled carbon nanotube–TiO 2 (SWCNT–TiO 2 ) hybrids that enables trace oxygen detection. Immobilization of red‐absorbing squaraine sensitizers on TiO 2 domains embedded within a conductive SWCNT network reversibly generates a photostationary charge‐transfer state under 628 nm excitation. Despite the low photon energy of red light, the hybrid architecture supports interfacial electron injection into TiO 2 and hole accumulation in the nanotube scaffold, while remaining electronically dormant in the dark. Interception of photogenerated electrons by O 2 perturbs this light‐induced state and converts excited‐state redox chemistry into a chemiresistive signal with ppb‐level sensitivity. This capability enables continuous monitoring of oxygen depletion in a sealed headspace during food spoilage. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, energy‐level alignment analysis, and charge‐carrier inversion experiments show that O 2 triggers light‐activated changes in SWCNT carrier density. These findings demonstrate that low‐energy optical excitation can gate chemical response in dye‐sensitized SWCNT–TiO 2 hybrids, establishing a design strategy for temporally controlled sensing and photoresponsive electronic function.
